articles.title: NFL Week 7 INSTANT reactions: Seahawks shut down Mahomes, J.J. McCarthy SHOCKS Texans
articles.summary: Nate Tice & Hayden Winks dive into their instant takeaways from Week 7 of NFL action.
articles.body:
Nate Tice & Hayden Winks dive into their instant takeaways from Week 7 of NFL action. The duo start with their reactions to the Seattle Seahawks handing the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss on Sunday night: how did Mike Macdonald shut down Kenneth Walker III?

Next, Nate & Hayden dive into their Pick 6, featuring six takeaways from NFL Week 7. Hayden highlights J.J. McCarthy's huge win for the New York Giants over the Houston Texans, the Atlanta Falcons taking down the undefeated San Francisco 49ers with a new-look offense and the Cincinnati Bengals riding a huge second half to victory over the Baltimore Ravens. Nate focuses on the Detroit Lions taking down the Green Bay Packers, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers steamrolling the Carolina Panthers and the Miami Dolphins getting their first win of the season and beating the New York Jets.

articles.title: NFL Week 7: A divisional duel in Detroit, and Aaron Rodgers keeps winning
articles.summary: Week 7 of the NFL season featured a Super Bowl contender getting back on track and a thrilling divisional showdown in the NFC North, plus another comeback win for one of the NFL’s most surprising teams.
articles.body: Week 7 of the NFL season featured a Super Bowl contender getting back on track and a thrilling divisional showdown in the NFC North, plus another comeback win for one of the NFL’s most surprising teams. Here’s what you need to know about from Sunday. The Lions won a wild one at home What a game between the Detroit Lions and the Green Bay Packers in the late window. The Lions won 20-17 on a walk-off field goal after a drama-filled affair that included controversial calls, plenty of offense and even an offensive lineman running a drag route. Both quarterbacks were dealing. Detroit’s Jared Goff completed 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards in the win, while Green Bay’s Jordan Love was 22 of 32 for 303 yards. Love could have had an even bigger day, but his receivers had multiple drops in big moments. The game was also filled with miscues. The Packers missed two field goals, both of which were shorter than 40 yards. Detroit, meanwhile, had two turnovers after not having given the ball away even once since Week 1. The fourth quarter was especially intense. The Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 from their own 24 but were stuffed on a run. Green Bay couldn’t take advantage on its ensuing possession, however. After they picked up only 5 yards, the Packers lined up for a 35-yard field goal, but Trey Smack’s kick was deflected. Detroit’s offense finally finished the job from there, going 71 yards and running out the clock for a game-winning kick by Jake Bates. The Lions improved to 4-2, while the Packers fell to 4-3. Can the Browns keep getting away with this? Cleveland improved to 5-2 after a last-minute, 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans. The Browns are not only one of the NFL’s most surprising teams; they are the league’s comeback kings so far this season. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has led a game-winning drive in each of the team’s five wins this year, and those five game-winning drives are the most by any Cleveland quarterback in a single season this century, per ESPN. The Browns got a breakout game from rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion, who had eight catches for 129 yards. Tight end Harold Fannin Jr. made a huge play late with a 36-yard catch and run to set up a game-winning field goal. Can Cleveland keep this up? All five of its wins have come by four points or less. The Browns have a negative-13 point differential despite their winning record. Cleveland keeps winning, but the margins are super thin. J.J. McCarthy gets his first win for the Giants A week after he threw 243 yards in relief of Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy got the start for New York and led the Giants to a 27-21 win over the Houston Texans in overtime. McCarthy played a clean game, completing 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards. He improved to 7-4 in his career as a starter, and New York is now 4-2-1 — and atop the NFC East. McCarthy got a huge boost from his rushing attack, as Cam Skattebo ran for 124 yards and a score, while former Texan Devin Singletary ran for the winning touchdown in the extra period. The Rams have a get-right game It’s been a frustrating season for Los Angeles, which entered Week 7 with a 2-4 record. The Rams’ last three losses came by a combined nine points, a sign the team was closer to the preseason favorite most assumed it would be. Los Angeles finally lived up to its potential in a 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The Rams scored 28 points in the first half alone, thanks in large part to a rushing attack that averaged 5.2 yards per rush en route to 199 yards. Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford was efficient, finishing the game with 195 yards on 23 of 29 passing. Los Angeles’ next three games are against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Washington Commanders and the Arizona Cardinals — an opportunity for the 3-4 Rams to get back over .500. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers keep winning After quarterback Aaron Rodgers looked every bit his age in a sluggish start to the season, the 42-year-old four-time MVP has led Pittsburgh to a 4-1 record in its last five games. The Steelers squeaked out a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in Paris in a game played without incident amid protests in France. Rodgers has completed at least 60% of his passes in each of the last three weeks, all of which were Pittsburgh wins. On Sunday, he even dialed back the clock to pick up a key first down late with his legs, effectively icing the game. The Steelers are tied with the Browns atop the AFC North, though Cleveland is in first place by virtue of a head-to-head tiebreaker. An undefeated falls, and a defeated rises The San Francisco 49ers fell to 6-1 in a 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. The 49ers entered injury-depleted (particularly at receiver) and then lost running back Christian McCaffrey during the game. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions, but it’s far from panic time in the Bay. Meanwhile, the Miami Dolphins picked up their first win of the season and the first career win for head coach Jeff Hafley. The Dolphins outlasted the New York Jets 28-25, and it’s possible losing to a previously winless Miami team puts Jets coach Aaron Glenn on a seat too hot to come back from.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor, Buckner, Nelson React to NFL Trade Rumors, Colts Losing and 'Frustration'
articles.summary: Three members of the Indianapolis Colts who are potentially on the trade block offered their thoughts following Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
Three members of the Indianapolis Colts who are potentially on the trade block offered their thoughts following Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

Heading into the game, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported teams are circling around Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.

With Indy now sitting at 2-5 on the season, a fire sale might be closer to happening.

"You come out, you play hard, you fight, and it always comes down to a couple plays," Taylor said of the Vikings game, per the Associated Press' Dave Campbell . "It's a very good team over there, but at the end of the day, I know we have the guys. We knew it was going to be a challenge, but you've got to think about how to find ways to just make one more play than your opponent."

Asked about his "level of frustration," Buckner responded as you'd expect and said he doesn't have a lot of answers to cure the Colts' woes:

"I just feel like everyone came to work and are doing their best," he said. "I don't know what else to say."

Indianapolis didn't lose Sunday through a lack of effort.

Taylor ran for 95 yards and a touchdown. The defense held Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray to 150 yards, and Minnesota didn't get its first touchdown until the fourth quarter.

But moral victories count for little when a team is sliding further away from the playoff picture. NFL.com puts the Colts' postseason probability at a paltry nine percent.

The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, and Indianapolis has two games before then. Should the team suffer two more losses, the makeshift front office might be resigned to selling off some valuable assets and starting over.

articles.title: “She’s been very secretive and selective": Gisele Bündchen’s comments about Tom Brady’s rumoured girlfriend Candice Swanepoel resurface
articles.summary: Tom Brady’s reported romance with supermodel Candice Swanepoel has drawn fresh attention to an unexpected connection between the new couple and his former
articles.body: Tom Brady’s reported romance with supermodel Candice Swanepoel has drawn fresh attention to an unexpected connection between the new couple and his former wife, Gisele Bündchen. While Brady and Swanepoel have yet to publicly confirm their relationship, reports suggest they have been dating for months. What makes the story more intriguing is Bündchen’s previous show of support for Swanepoel, offering a glimpse into a connection that existed long before the latest dating rumours emerged. Her past comments are now gaining renewed attention as interest grows in Brady’s personal life following his 2022 divorce.Gisele Bündchen’s support for Candice Swanepoel goes back yearsBündchen’s connection with Swanepoel extends beyond their shared careers in the modelling industry. The Brazilian supermodel previously praised Swanepoel’s swimwear brand, Tropic of C, showing that their professional relationship had a friendly side.In December 2019, Bündchen shared a photograph of herself wearing a swimsuit from the brand. She also publicly thanked Swanepoel for the gift, making her appreciation clear.“Thank you @angelcandices for the beautiful @tropicofc bikini. I loved it!,” Bündchen wrote.The gesture offered a small but notable example of Bündchen supporting another model’s business. Swanepoel, who built her career through major fashion campaigns and Victoria’s Secret, later expanded her work into swimwear with Tropic of C.Bündchen’s earlier endorsement has become relevant again because of the reported relationship between Swanepoel and Brady. However, her past praise should not be taken as confirmation of her views on the alleged romance. There is no indication in the reported comments that she was addressing any future relationship between the two.Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel reportedly keep romance privateAccording to reports cited by The Spun, Brady and Swanepoel have been spending considerable time together in Miami, where both have connections. A source quoted by People described the arrangement as convenient because they live in the same city.“They both live in Miami, so it’s very convenient,” an insider told People Sunday.The source also claimed that the pair had been dating for months and were careful about keeping their meetings private.“They’re spending a lot of time together. Candice and Tom have been dating for months,” the source continued. “She’s been very secretive and selective about who she’s told about their dating.”“When they have met up, they’ve gone [to great] lengths not to be spotted,” the source added.Brady, 49, shares two children with Bündchen, whom he married in 2009 before their divorce in 2022. He is also a father to a son from his previous relationship with actress Bridget Moynahan.The former NFL quarterback has previously spoken about the demands of balancing work and family life.“You know what? I don’t have much time for a personal life or much time for myself, but I love working and I love my kids,” he told People at the time.“I like to be busy and try to really stay fulfilled in the things I’m doing,” he continued. “So I’m working on some really cool projects and I’m involved with some great teams of people that are doing some really positive things.”For now, Brady and Swanepoel’s reported romance remains unconfirmed, while Bündchen’s past support for the model adds an interesting layer to the developing story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'S--t, We Lost,' Kenneth Walker III Addresses Not Shaking Hands with Seahawks After Chiefs' Loss
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III wasn't in a mood to chat with some of his old teammates following Sunday's 20-3 defeat to the Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III wasn't in a mood to chat with some of his old teammates following Sunday's 20-3 defeat to the Seattle Seahawks.

Walker avoided the traditional postgame handshakes and headed straight for the locker room.

"S--t, we lost," he said matter-of-factly, per ESPN's Nate Taylor . "I was frustrated. That's about it. I [saw] them over there celebrating and s--t. That's about it."

Beyond coming out on the losing end, Walker had by far his worst game of the season. He ran for just 36 yards on 14 carries.

Walker didn't have a bitter divorce from the Seahawks in the offseason. He parlayed his Super Bowl MVP into a nice contract with the Chiefs and a bigger role in Kansas City that he was likely to have in Seattle.

There wasn't so much a revenge aspect at play as there was a straightforward challenge before the reigning champions. Safety Nick Emmanwori relished the opportunity to keep one of the league's top rushers in check.

"I definitely did want to hold him under 100 [yards]," Emmanwori said. "I don't really listen to all the media noise, but that was my motivation. I know a lot of dudes on the defense, that was their motivation, too, to stop him under 100 and play lights out on defense. I think we did that."

Walker is unlikely to get another crack at Seattle since that would mean facing off with the Seahawks in Super Bowl LXI.

Instead, he may channel his frustration from Sunday against the remaining opponents on the Chiefs' schedule.

articles.title: "Nothing is happening”: Tyreek Hill faces major setback in Chiefs reunion hopes as Kansas City weighs injury risks
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill’s potential return to the Kansas City Chiefs has hit a significant roadblock, leaving fans wondering whether the explosive wide receiver will
articles.body: Tyreek Hill’s potential return to the Kansas City Chiefs has hit a significant roadblock, leaving fans wondering whether the explosive wide receiver will wear the red and gold again. What once looked like a promising reunion has lost momentum as concerns over his recovery continue to shape the conversation. With the Chiefs winning games and Patrick Mahomes leading the offence, Kansas City faces a difficult choice: take a chance on a familiar star or trust the players already on the roster. For Hill, the bigger challenge remains proving he can return to the field at his best.Why the Chiefs are hesitant to sign Tyreek HillKansas City emerged as a possible destination for Hill after injuries disrupted its receiving group. Rashee Rice suffered a hamstring setback, while Tyquan Thornton sustained a serious ankle injury. Those setbacks created speculation that the Chiefs might look to a proven playmaker to strengthen their offence.However, Hill’s health remains the biggest obstacle. The 32-year-old suffered a dislocated left knee and multiple ligament tears while playing for the Miami Dolphins during Week 4 of the 2025 NFL season. His injury required two surgeries, making his road back to professional football particularly challenging.Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has offered encouraging updates about his client’s rehabilitation and readiness to explore opportunities with NFL teams. Yet positive training reports cannot replace the medical assessments teams need before committing to a player recovering from such a serious injury.Hill built his reputation on elite speed, sharp changes of direction and the ability to turn short passes into game-changing plays. Those qualities make him dangerous, but they also raise questions about how quickly he can regain his previous form.Without a clear medical assessment and a confirmed return timeline, Kansas City may be unwilling to take that risk.Andy Reid’s Tyreek Hill update offers little hope of a reunionChiefs head coach Andy Reid has done little to fuel expectations of a reunion. When asked about the speculation surrounding available players, Reid indicated that “nothing is happening” on the Tyreek Hill front.The comments suggest Kansas City is not preparing to rush into a deal, despite the team's earlier need for additional receiving options.Mahomes has also given the Chiefs reason to remain patient. He has started the 2026 campaign strongly, distributing the ball to targets such as Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. That production gives the coaching staff less reason to disrupt its current offensive plans for a player whose availability remains uncertain.Roster planning is another consideration. Bringing Hill back would require the team to assess his conditioning, recovery progress and ability to handle the demands of an NFL season. Promoting players who already understand Reid’s system could offer a more straightforward solution.Still, the situation could change if Kansas City suffers more injuries or Hill receives medical clearance sooner than expected.For now, Hill remains a free agent, and the Chiefs appear content to move forward without him. A reunion is not impossible, but the former Kansas City star must first overcome the uncertainty surrounding his recovery before any serious move becomes realistic.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Josh Simmons and Andy Reid’s clash or Seattle Seahawks’ defense in Kenneth Walker III’s absence? What cost Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City Chiefs their first 2026 NFL season loss
articles.summary: Josh Simmons kept his legs on the table during a team meeting. Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told him to keep them down.
articles.body: Josh Simmons kept his legs on the table during a team meeting. Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told him to keep them down. Simmons admitted that he had a hip and back problem causing him discomfort, which was why he kept his legs on the table.A heated exchange took place between the coach and the player. Simmons reportedly refused to obey Reid, prompting Patrick Mahomes to intervene. Mahomes asked Simmons to leave the meeting, and Simmons left.Now that we know the whole story, the timing of its occurrence - just before the Week 7 game of the 2026 NFL season - makes us wonder: did it break the Kansas City Chiefs’ five-game winning streak?Or was it the dominant Seattle Seahawks defense alone that did not let Mahomes move even an inch? They even lost their own Super Bowl-winning rusher, Kenneth Walker III.Josh Simmons’ heated exchange raises Chiefs’ loss questionsThe Kansas City Chiefs suffered their first defeat at the hands of the 2025 Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, after a frustrating 20-3 loss on Sunday night in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense struggled, while Seattle’s dominant defensive performance proved to be the defining factor in the Week 7 clash.However, it was the reported heated exchange between second-year offensive tackle Josh Simmons and head coach Andy Reid - and the later alleged involvement of Patrick Mahomes - that preluded this heartbreaking loss.After the clash, Reid reportedly told Simmons to leave the meeting and seek treatment, a move that Mahomes supported. Simmons later apologized to the coach and the team leadership for how he handled the situation.However, Simmons was placed on injured reserve immediately thereafter because of a bulging disc in his lower back. Andy Reid dismissed any notion that the heated exchange caused the roster move. He emphasized instead that Simmons needed to recover from his injury.Nevertheless, this incident could have caused the team to lose its spirit. If a player was injured and treated a certain way, it could impact the squad’s overall morale. It raises the question: what if another player were experiencing discomfort and needed to keep their legs in a comfortable position?Chiefs Patrick Mahomes’ offensive strugglesPatrick Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards and threw an interception. He threw zero touchdowns and gained a 58.3 passer rating.The Kansas City Chiefs managed only 213 total yards of offense. The offense struggled to sustain drives, recording just 11 first downs and converting only 3 of 11 third-down opportunities.Kansas City’s only points came after kicker Harrison Butker made a 50-yard field goal in the third quarter of the Week 7 clash [he missed two other attempts]. Josh Simmons’ absence was deeply felt, as was Jaylon Moore’s unavailability due to a concussion suffered during Week 6 win against the Los Angeles Chargers.Seattle Seahawks’ surprising defensive dominanceFor the first five games of the 2026 NFL season [Week 5 was bye for the Chiefs], Patrick Mahomes established himself as an unstoppable threat despite having only recently recovered from an ACL tear.In those initial games, five teams lost to the Chiefs. But when the Seattle Seahawks came to face one of the NFL’s most dangerous quarterbacks, the Super Bowl-winning team’s defense delivered a statement performance.Sam Darnold-led Seattle limited Mahomes’ team to just three points. They controlled the line of scrimmage and persistently prevented Mahomes from establishing an offensive rhythm.The unit also prevented individual 100-yard rushers. The Seahawks’ disciplined tackling and calculating defense forced the Chiefs into difficult passing situations.The victory was more than just crucial for Seattle - who had been waiting a long time for a rebound. They had endured just one victory and three losses in nearly a month’s time. With the win, they improved their 2026 season record to 4-3, while the Chiefs fell to 5-1.Kenneth Walker III’s Seahawks returnKenneth Walker III played against his former team, the Seattle Seahawks, in a Week 7 matchup. The running back was not offered enough money to remain with the Seahawks, despite winning a Super Bowl and earning MVP honours for them just last season.Walker entered the 2026 free agency. The Seahawks reportedly did not offer him a contract extension because they wanted to prioritize salary cap flexibility.They did not engage in a bidding war for a running back too. The Kansas City Chiefs capitalized on that by signing Walker to a blockbuster deal [three-year, $43.05 million contract].However, when it mattered the most, Walker couldn’t cast his magic. He had been at the heart of all five wins for Kansas City; but was limited to just 36 rushing yards on 14 carries against his former team in the Week 7 loss.Facing a vacant running back spot without Walker while Zach Charbonnet was recovering, the Seahawks signed Emanuel Wilson after Wilson entered free agency following his departure from the Green Bay Packers.Wilson did not find it intimidating to play against a former Seahawk [Walker]; he rushed for 100 yards on 24 attempts, helping the home team secure a firm hold on the game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brutal Stats for Aaron Glenn Go Viral as Fans Put Jets HC on Hot Seat After Loss to Dolphins
articles.summary: After losing to the previously winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday, New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is on the wrong side of history.
articles.body:
After losing to the previously winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday, New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is on the wrong side of history.

Fans on social media couldn't help but call out Glenn's 0-8 record in AFC East games and his poor point differential in the final two minutes of the first half:

The Dolphins entered Sunday's game with a 0-5 record, but from the outset, it looked like it was the Jets who were searching for their first win. Miami jumped out to a 21-7 lead in the first half and held on for a 28-25 victory, dropping New York to 2-5 this year.

Since Glenn took over as head coach prior to the 2025 campaign, the Jets have gone 5-19. New York was known to be a rebuilding team that wouldn't take a quick fix, but its lack of progress in Glenn's second year at the helm is alarming.

After the game, Glenn accepted the blame for his team's poor performance, particularly on defense after he took over as the defensive play-caller this season.

"I'm highly disappointed in myself," Glenn told reporters . "First and foremost, defensively, we did not play well in the first half."

Still, Glenn expressed optimism that the Jets will be able to turn things around.

"I understand the fans' frustration -- I really do. I promise you, I do -- but the thing is, I do feel like, man, this program is going in the right direction," he said.

The Jets will try to get back on track when they host the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) in Week 8.

articles.title: Ex-NFL star says police aimed gun at him in front of his daughters amid incident with alleged reckless drivers
articles.summary: Footage shows a Southlake Texas police officer aiming a gun at Dez Bryant during a confrontation that ended with the former Cowboy in handcuffs.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: Former Dallas Cowboys star Dez Bryant says a police officer aimed a gun at him in front of his daughters Sunday after a confrontation with a man he alleges threatened to shoot him following an encounter with two men who he accused or reckless driving. The incident resulted in Bryant receiving an assault citation, but began when the two men cut him off in traffic and put him in a dangerous situation, and he just tried to tell them to drive safer, he said. Footage provided to OutKick by Bryant showed an officer aiming a gun in Bryant’s direction. Bryant is also seen lying on the ground in handcuffs alongside the two other men in Southlake, Texas. Bryant ended up at the same parking lot with them, where acknowledged knocking a phone from one man’s hand during their argument, but disputed how police handled the encounter and questioned why he received a citation after reporting that he had been threatened. ARIZONA STATE CHEERLEADER CHARGED AFTER CONFRONTATION WITH POLICE CAUGHT ON VIRAL VIDEO "I was really more so concerned about my children, you know, looking at their dad, you know, being on the ground with a gun pointed at me," Bryant said. The citation reviewed by OutKick lists "Assault by Contact" and identifies the incident location as 2251 E. Southlake Blvd., the same address listed for Chiloso Mexican Bistro. It marks "Arrest: No" and instructs Bryant to appear at Southlake Municipal Court on or before Nov. 20 at 5 p.m. Bryant said the confrontation began after he encountered two vehicles whose occupants appeared to be interacting with one another at a traffic light. He accused the drivers of cutting him off and continuing to drive recklessly as they arrived at the restaurant, where he was also headed. Bryant said he told them to stop, acknowledging that he used profanity. He said an argument followed with one of the men, whom the former wide receiver described as a young adult. TITANS COACH PASSIONATELY DEFENDS JORDAN ELLIOTT AFTER GUN-RELATED INCIDENT LED TO RELEASE "He go to threatening me and basically saying, um, he’ll insinuate that he’ll, you know, he’ll shoot me or whatever," Bryant said. Bryant said he responded with a warning of his own. "You pull that gun, I’m telling you right now, you better use it because if you don’t I’m going to do something to you," he recalled telling the man. Asked whether the man actually drew a weapon, Bryant said: "No, he didn’t pull a gun out on me." Bryant said the man instead pulled out his phone and began recording him. "I told him, you know, get the phone off me," Bryant said. "So what I ended up doing is I knocked the phone out of his hand." The man then said he would call police, according to Bryant, who said he encouraged him to do so because he believed officers would investigate the alleged threat. Bryant said a responding officer drew a gun and ordered them to the ground. He said his girlfriend arrived with his two daughters and began recording the encounter. ICE SHOOTING ROCKS AUSTIN AS DEMOCRAT DEMANDS BODYCAM VIDEO, INDEPENDENT PROBE "I get on the ground," Bryant said. "My lady pulled up, she got my children, and they seen everything that’s going on." According to Bryant, officers handcuffed the men, questioned them separately and placed him in a police vehicle before releasing him with the citation. He said the other men were allowed to leave. Bryant alleged that police relied on the other man’s phone recording without adequately investigating what preceded it. He said he asked officers to review surrounding surveillance footage, including any available video of the driving that led to the confrontation. "I would rather you guys take us all down to the police station and do the proper investigation instead of just taking somebody else, you know, side," Bryant said. "I felt like it was very one-sided." Bryant also claims an officer told him that he had to be "the bigger person." Under Texas law, assault involving offensive or provocative physical contact is generally a Class C misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of up to $500. The citation does not identify a specific statutory subsection. Bryant repeatedly described his actions as self-defense. Texas law makes that determination dependent on the circumstances, including whether someone reasonably believed force was immediately necessary to protect against another person’s use or attempted use of unlawful force. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Bryant emphasized that he has longstanding positive relationships with individual Southlake officers, including one associated with his son’s Southlake Carroll football team. "Every time I see him, we talk ball. We just talk about the regular things," Bryant said of that officer. "It’s always been good. This situation was just extremely unfortunate." Bryant played eight seasons with Dallas, earning three Pro Bowl selections and All-Pro honors in 2014. He finished his Cowboys tenure with 531 catches, 7,459 receiving yards and 73 receiving touchdowns. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! He said his standing in the Southlake community, particularly among children who look up to him, motivated him to speak publicly about the encounter. "My reputation mean everything to me," Bryant said. Asked what he wanted from law enforcement moving forward, Bryant called for fairness and a thorough investigation. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody with respect," he said. "Do your due diligence on what’s actually going on." OutKick has reached out to the City of Southlake for a comment on behalf of the police department.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 8 Waiver-Wire Pickups, Rankings and Box Score Stat Projections
articles.summary: By this point on the NFL calendar, team identities seem fully formed or well on their way to becoming that.
articles.body:
By this point on the NFL calendar, team identities seem fully formed or well on their way to becoming that.

And that probably rings even truer for fantasy rosters than it does for their real-life counterparts, since fantasy campaigns are completed long before a Super Bowl champion is crowned.

Most managers should have a good sense of just how competitive their clubs are and can be. They might also have an idea of what needs to happen to take the next step.

Whether that's deft lineup management or savvy dealings on the waiver wire, this early Week 8 guide should help on both fronts.

Waiver-wire target: Michael Penix Jr., ATL (at TB)

Penix may not produce the loudest volume around, but the Falcons are starting to crank things up a bit. He has thrown at least 32 passes in three consecutive contests. More importantly, he has tallied seven touchdown throws against a single interception during this stretch.

Projected stats: 21-of-32 for 227 yards, two touchdowns

Waiver-wire target: Jonah Coleman, DEN (vs. KC)

Coleman suited up for the first time Sunday since a sprained ankle in Week 2 sent him to injured reserve, and the fourth-round rokie played like he was aiming to make up for lost time. His nine carries yielded 54 rushing yards, and he hauled in both of his targets for another 15 yards. Even in a crowded backfield, that's efficiency worth noting.

Projected stats: 12 carries for 53 yards, two receptions for 17 yards, one touchdown

Waiver-wire target: Omar Cooper Jr., NYJ (vs. LV)

Cooper flashed in Week 6, and the fantasy community left him largely unclaimed, perhaps needing to see more evidence of his roster-worthiness. So, the rookie first-rounder delivered exactly that, turning in his second straight effort with triple-digit yardage (five catches for 115 yards) and a score.

Projected stats: Six receptions for 83 yards, one touchdown

articles.title: 'Sucks,' Patrick Mahomes Honest After Kenneth Walker, Chiefs Lose Revenge Game to Seahawks
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes doesn't think he and the rest of the offense did enough to supplement running back Kenneth Walker III in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes doesn't think he and the rest of the offense did enough to supplement running back Kenneth Walker III in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.

"We have to help him. That's the biggest thing," Mahomes said after the game, per ESPN's Nate Taylor . "When they put so many eggs in that basket of stopping the run game, we have to have the play-action game and the movement game to be able to throw the ball. If we're not providing that, they're going to continue to put those guys up at the line of scrimmage. That's hard for the run game."

Walker ran for 36 yards on 14 carries against his old team, his worst performance so far since signing with the Chiefs.

Kansas City couldn't get much going on offense period. It finished with 213 total yards and didn't manage once to get inside the red zone. Taylor noted this was the first time it had happened in one of Mahomes' starts.

"We didn't execute, especially around that midfield area," the two-time MVP said. "It kept us away from a lot of points, or at least enough points to be competitive. We've got to learn from it. You've got to feel it. This sucks. You don't want to perform like this in prime time."

Week 8 presents the Chiefs with an opportunity to rediscover their groove.

The Denver Broncos allowed the second-fewest yards per game in 2025 but have gone backward. They surrendered 392 yards to Kansas City in an opening-week defeat. Walker had 173 yards on the ground and averaged 7.5 yards per carry.

Maybe this is when Denver's defense finally wakes up. Otherwise, it could be a long day against a Chiefs offense with a point to prove.

articles.title: Week 8 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by Jonah Coleman, Omar Cooper Jr., Caleb Douglas
articles.summary: Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season is almost finished.
articles.body:
Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season is almost finished.

If you're somehow not in need of roster reinforcements, congratulations for being among the most fortunate managers in all of fantasy football.

But since you opened this article, you're probably in the same camp as the rest of us: looking to plug holes that keep springing every week due to injuries, byes or the brutal combination of the two. So, let's find some viable plug-and-play replacements who are readily available with roster rates under 50 percent, per FantasyPros .

Jonah Coleman, RB, Denver Broncos (35% Rostered)

There haven't been many sources of inspiration among waiver-wire running backs but Coleman has a chance to break that mold a bit.

Granted, he's a rookie fourth-rounder in a crowded backfield, so expectations are probably best tempered. And a lot of this stems from a Week 7 showing that didn't include 70 scrimmage yards or a score.

That said, he looked pretty awesome in his return from injured reserve, as he needed just 11 touches (nine carries, two catches) to tally 69 scrimmage yards. It was the kind of jolt this offense has struggled to find from its running game, and it sounds like it could get Coleman into more prominent position in the pecking order.

If Coleman somehow grabs control of this backfield, he could be a real impact addition to any fantasy roster.

Omar Cooper Jr., WR, New York Jets (39% Rostered)

Cooper delivered an eye-opener in Week 6 (six receptions for 103 yards and a touchdown), but fantasy managers apparently needed more convincing.

After he effectively copy-pasted the production Week 7 (five receptions for 115 yards and a score), you'd think the convincing is covered now.

He has big-play burst (he's had at least a 30-yard catch in every game he's played), but he is seeing enough volume to avoid the volatility of a boom-or-bust downfield specialist. If the Jets are going to involve him, it looks like he's going to deliver.

Maybe it won't always be this productive, but the mere chance that it could be should have him rocketing above the roster percentage threshold for waiver-wire talks.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Miami Dolphins (13% Rostered)

If you're aiming for security on the waiver wire, Douglas shouldn't be the priority. There just isn't a lot of certainty with this passing game in general, and he has only seen three targets in each of his last two games.

If, however, you're in the market for upside, then you should probably have an interest in seeing where this might head. Because his return from a three-game absence was loaded with electricity, as he turned those three targets into two catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns.

Again, it's fair to question how often this passing game can produce big plays, but when it does, there's a good chance Douglas will be involved. He's a 6'4", 205-pounder with sub-4.40 speed. He absolutely aces the eye test.

Is consistency going to be part of his fantasy profile? Probably not, or at least not this early into his NFL career. That said, his big games could be week-winners, and he doesn't need to a ton of opportunities to put one together. If you can spare the space, or are desperate enough to go the lottery-ticket route, rostering Douglas and seeing what will happen makes a lot of sense.

articles.title: How Amon-Ra St. Brown’s apparent kick at an NFL official left Green Bay Packers fans furious after Devonte Wyatt’s 15-Yard penalty
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers had plenty to be upset about after their 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions on October 25, 2026.
articles.body: The Green Bay Packers had plenty to be upset about after their 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions on October 25, 2026. But one third-quarter call quickly became the biggest talking point. Amon-Ra St. Brown appeared to kick umpire Terry Killens Jr. in the midsection during a tackle. Yet officials penalized Packers defensive lineman Devonte Wyatt for unnecessary roughness, leaving Green Bay fans questioning the decision.The flag gave Detroit a fresh set of downs near the goal line and helped set up a touchdown. Packers coach Matt LaFleur also challenged the officials' explanation after the game. While Green Bay had other chances to win, the unusual sequence added another layer of frustration to a divisional loss.Why the Amon-Ra St. Brown incident sparked outrage among Packers fansThe play began when Lions quarterback Jared Goff completed a four-yard pass to St. Brown in the third quarter. Packers linebacker Isaiah McDuffie tackled the receiver, who appeared to try to get back up. Wyatt then brought St. Brown down again.As the players collided, St. Brown's cleat appeared to strike Killens in the stomach. The umpire fell to the ground but threw a flag while lying on his back.Officials called unnecessary roughness on Wyatt, moving Detroit from a third-and-seven at Green Bay's 23-yard line to a first-and-10 at the 11. Two plays later, Goff found Jameson Williams for a 10-yard touchdown. The score put Detroit ahead 17-14.After the game on October 25, referee Alex Moore explained the call to reporters. He said officials considered the play over before Wyatt made the second tackle.“We ruled that the play was over,” Moore said. He added that Wyatt made an additional tackle with force after the play had ended. Moore's explanation focused on Wyatt's actions, not the apparent contact between St. Brown's cleat and the umpire.Matt LaFleur questions the explanation as Detroit wins lateLaFleur also disagreed with the officials' account. Speaking to reporters after the Packers' loss on October 25, the Green Bay coach said he had not heard a whistle before Wyatt made the tackle.“There was no whistle blown and the guy continued to run … so our guys continued to play, too,” LaFleur said, according to the Packers' official recap.Still, Green Bay had a chance to take control late in the game. Trey Smack kicked a 43-yard field goal to tie the score at 17-17 in the fourth quarter. The Packers later lined up for a 35-yard attempt, but Lions defender D.J. Wonnum got a fingertip on the kick and sent it wide.Detroit then drove into field-goal range. Jake Bates converted from 22 yards as time expired to seal the 20-17 win at Ford Field.The result moved the Lions to 4-2 and dropped the Packers to 4-3. Green Bay fans continued to criticize the disputed penalty online, with some questioning why Wyatt received the flag after St. Brown appeared to hit the official.The call did not decide the game on its own, but it gave Detroit a valuable scoring chance and left the Packers with fresh questions about the officiating.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Coach Reacts to Aaron Rodgers, McCarthy 'Calling Each Other F--king Ass--les' on TV
articles.summary: After improving to 5-2 this season, the Pittsburgh Steelers appear to have moved on from the spat between veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy from earlier in the year.
articles.body:
After improving to 5-2 this season, the Pittsburgh Steelers appear to have moved on from the spat between veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy from earlier in the year.

The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to an NFL coach who praised Rodgers and McCarthy for overcoming the early-season turmoil after they were caught exchanging expletives back and forth during a Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns.

"They are calling each other f--king ass--les and embarrassing each other on national TV, but I wouldn't be surprised if they went and got a beer on (East) Carson Street afterward," the coach said. "They are bonded forever."

The Steelers won their third straight game on Sunday, defeating the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in Paris. Despite a lackluster offensive performance , Pittsburgh's defense did enough to secure the victory.

The coach went on to tell Sando, "They actually could win a playoff game," pointing to the team's grind-it-out approach.

"This thing has a chance," the coach said. "The strong defense (fifth in expected points added per play) and run game (fourth in EPA per rush) are what make it really compelling."

The Steelers will try to continue their winning ways when they face the Cleveland Browns (5-2) with first place in the AFC North on the line in Week 8.

articles.title: Latest Peyton Manning-Colts Rumors from Dan Patrick After Chris Ballard Fired as GM
articles.summary: After firing general manager Chris Ballard, the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly still interested in handing the position to legendary former quarterback Peyton Manning, but there are a lot of hurdles in the way.
articles.body:
After firing general manager Chris Ballard, the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly still interested in handing the position to legendary former quarterback Peyton Manning, but there are a lot of hurdles in the way.

Dan Patrick, who was the first to report on the Colts' interest in Manning, asked his source, "Did I whiff?" and he received a detailed response.

"Not at all. They have talked, and as you already indicated, ultimately the timing is not right, but the interest is there," the source told Patrick. "Family and business interests are the immediate priorities for Peyton. The Colts still have structuring to do, true football and business sides, and it all goes to the Irsays. That's in the process, it's not done yet. Again, timing is an issue here. Peyton ultimately indicated he wants Omaha Productions 'fully stood up.' And ideally wants his kids in, or if possible, beyond college. He'd consider consulting before that, but nothing more."

Patrick needed to clarify his reporting after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that the Colts "have not approached Manning about their vacant GM job, nor would the Hall of Fame quarterback be expected to be interested in the position."

"Manning would be willing to listen and consider any NFL opportunities at any time, but the Colts have not discussed any of those possibilities with him, according to sources," Schefter added. "It's possible that some could come in the future, sources said, but those discussions likely would involve higher-profile positions similar to the ones that other former NFL quarterbacks have accepted with other franchises."

Patrick's source also indicated that Manning would not hastily accept the Colts' GM position amid his family and media obligations.

"Peyton is 50. He's got both options. He has time," the source told Patrick. "They don't intend to share this publicly. Former GM Bill Polian was in town last week…and encouraged the Peyton Manning approach."

The Colts fell to 2-5 following Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings, so the team could use some positive news in its GM search to provide some optimism for the future. For now, it sounds like Manning is in no rush to take the job.

articles.body:

The officials flagged him for the 15-yard foul after he lowered his head to brace for contact from Texans safety M.J. Stewart.

After the game, Skattebo called out what he believes is a level of hypocrisy:

articles.title: Vikings' Kyler Murray makes never-seen-before NFL history with undefeated record
articles.summary: This is quite an impressive record for Kyler Murray to set in his NFL career.
articles.body:
Throughout NFL history, there have been plenty of incredible quarterbacks to play for multiple teams in their careers. While not all switched teams while in their prime, there have been a lot of noteworthy QBs to play for multiple franchises in their careers.

Kyler Murray, now with the Minnesota Vikings , might just be another name to mention as a prominent starting QB to switch teams in the middle of his career. But after the Vikings' Week 7 win over the Indianapolis Colts , his name belongs in NFL history books.

As OptaSTATS shared, Murray and the Vikings' Week 7 win kept the team undefeated at 6-0, and with no other undefeated teams remaining, Murray has now become the only QB ever to lead two different teams to the last remaining undefeated team in the NFL.

Kyler Murray makes undefeated NFL history never seen before

"Nobody else in the Super Bowl era has been the primary starting QB for the NFL's last remaining unbeaten team with 2 different franchises," OptaSTATS shared.

In 2021, Murray was quarterbacking the NFL's last unbeaten team with the Arizona Cardinals . Five years later, the 2026 Vikings are the last team without a loss in the NFL.

No other quarterback in NFL history, since the Super Bowl era began over 60 years ago, has ever led a team to be the last undefeated squad in the NFL with two separate franchises.

This was only possible in 2026 thanks to the San Francisco 49ers losing to the Atlanta Falcons in a big upset, dropping to 6-1 for the year.

Then, later in the night, the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs lost their first game of the season, failing to produce much offense against the Seattle Seahawks .

While there might be things to worry about with this Vikings team, and that 6-0 record might not tell the full story, there's no denying that this is a good team, and that Murray has now made some never-before-seen NFL history as well.

articles.title: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren knew Saints sucked at run defense, so he ran it down their throats
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers had running back Rico Dowdle available to play for their NFL Paris Game against the New Orleans Saints. As a result, they were able t...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers had running back Rico Dowdle available to play for their NFL Paris Game against the New Orleans Saints. As a result, they were able to effectively execute their gameplan of utilizing their ground game.

Steelers running back Jaylen Warren confirmed that the Steelers' strategy was as simple as them taking advantage of the Saints' shortcoming .

"We knew what we know about them. So we wanted to use our strengths against their weaknesses," Warren said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Steelers finished with 148 rushing yards against the Saints, which is a season-high. Warren was responsible for 101 of those yards on 18 carries, which were a season-high. Meanwhile, Dowdle got 41 yards on nine carries.

Whether it's basic stats or advanced analytics , the numbers show that the Saints just aren't a very good run defense. That was on display against the Steelers, who were smart to keep things simple and just attack that soft spot in New Orleans' armor.

With Dowdle back to form a two-headed monster with Warren in the backfield, the Steelers have the potential to be a potent running attack. Warren is having a fantastic season to date , with 561 rushing yards on 5.5 yards per carry. He's also been brilliant as a pass catcher, with 294 yards on 24 catches.

As Dowdle has shown in his back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons with the Dallas Cowboys and Carolina Panthers, he is capable of being a reliable featured back. If he can pick up more carries while Warren continues to be a dual-threat running back, the Steelers' backfield figures to be a major strength moving forward.

articles.title: Robert Saleh on Titans defense vs Browns: 'Our tackling sucked'
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh is displeased with how his defense played in the team's loss to the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans first-year coach Robert Saleh continued to vent on his defense, which gave up 491 yards on offense, a day after his team fell to 1-6 with 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns at Nissan Stadium .

His defense's effort on the last drive of the game resulted in a 32-yard field goal as time expired to give the Browns the win on Oct. 25. Yes, what many consider a blown false start call that preceded the final kick contributed to the loss.

Inside Titans vs Browns. Cam Ward, Jeffery Simmons and our best photos

But that didn't change Saleh's opinion of his team's performance.

"Our tackling sucked yesterday," he said during his weekly morning Zoom meeting with reporters on Oct. 26. "The tackling on the last play of the game sucked, and talking to the referees about a guy being offsides is pointless.

Saleh also cited the Titans ' inability to rush the quarterback and stop the run as more reasons why the Titans, seven games into the season, sit second in the 2027 NFL Draft order , according to Tankathon.com .

"Right now we have a finishing problem," Saleh said.

The Titans play the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) on the road Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS).

Titans coach Robert Saleh defends Cam Ward

While his defense didn't defend well against the Browns, giving up 491 yards of total offense, Saleh did defend his quarterback, Cam Ward.

Ward, as he has most of the season, struggled through the first three quarters but woke up in time to give the Titans a chance to win. Ward's third-and-12 connection to Carnell Tate on the Titans' touchdown drive that tied the score 24-all late in the fourth.

Inside Tennessee Titans vs Derrick Henry, Ravens in NFL Week 4 game

"I thought he played a good game, not an exceptional game," Saleh said. "He has things he has to fix.

"You can't possibly watch that film and say Cam Ward did not play good, winning football. You can't. ... If anyone's trying to pin that loss on him, you're just trying to make (expletive) up."

One of the things Saleh said Ward, who was 20-for-31 for 181 yards, zero touchdowns and an interception, needs to improve is his footwork.

"Old habits are hard to break, especially in the heat of battle," Saleh said. "When the bullets are flying and things get real, sometimes you revert back to old habits."

Paul Skrbina is a sports enterprise reporter covering the Predators, Titans, Nashville SC, local colleges and local sports for The Tennessean. Reach him at pskrbina@tennessean.com and on the X platform (formerly known as Twitter) @paulskrbina .
